text:
Utah took 80 shot attempts to Boston's 35 and piled up 4.5 expected goals to the Bruins' 2.32, and still lost 6-1 at TD Garden. The simulated replays of every shot give UTA the win 81 percent of the time. The night turned on the power play: Boston scored on three of four chances, Utah went 0 for 7, and the Bruins converted chances that were rarely good ones. Casey Mittelstadt opened the scoring in the first period on a shot with a 6 percent chance of going in, and Mason Lohrei's goal at 15:51 carried the same 6 percent.

David Pastrnak did the most damage with the man advantage, scoring twice (one in each of the first two periods) and adding two assists, which made him first star. Morgan Geekie scored on a slap shot at 7:57 of the second for a 5-0 lead, and Matthew Poitras made it 6-0 on a wrist shot at 14:08. Boston's lead was built almost entirely on special teams, and the Bruins' even-strength expected goals (1.93) trailed Utah's 3.27 by a wide margin.

Jeremy Swayman is the other reason the score looks the way it does. He faced 37 shots, allowed one goal on 4.5 expected, and finished 3.5 goals better than average. Utah's goaltending went the other way, with Sebastian Cossa and Karel Vejmelka each allowing three on far fewer expected. Jack McBain finally beat Swayman at 9:48 of the third, a 45 percent chance, the best look of the night to go in.
